the traditional beliefs and stories of a people

normalIntro.en: Ethnology is ethnos plus logos: a reasoned account laid out across many peoples at once.
normalIntro.cn: ethnology 是 ethnos 加 logos：把有理据的论说同时铺展在许多民族之上。

normal.en: Ethno- marks a people, as it does in ethnic and ethnography.
normal.cn: ethno- 标记「民族」，ethnic 与 ethnography 也是如此。

normal.en: The ending -logy means the study of, as in biology.
normal.cn: 词尾 -logy 表示「……学」，biology 也是这样。

normal.en: An ethnologist compares, while an ethnographer describes.
normal.cn: ethnologist 做比较，ethnographer 做描述。

normal.en: Ethnological museums arrange objects by people and by region.
normal.cn: 民族学博物馆按民族与地区陈列器物。

normal.en: Compare -graphy and -logy: writing one people, versus reasoning about many.
normal.cn: 对比 -graphy 与 -logy：一个是写下一个民族，一个是对许多民族作论说。

abstract.en: See a long table with the languages and kinship terms of many peoples laid out side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，上面并排摊着许多民族的语言与亲属称谓，对应第 1 个义项的「比较研究」。

abstract.en: See lines drawn on a map of migrations, arrows meeting and splitting over the centuries.
abstract.cn: 想象一张迁徙地图上画出的线条，箭头在数百年间汇聚又分叉，对应第 2 个义项的「起源与分布」。

abstract.en: See one shelf in a library given wholly to a single northern people.
abstract.cn: 想象图书馆里整整一层书架只放关于某一个北方民族的研究，对应第 3 个义项的「区域知识」。

examples.en: Ethnology compares the kinship systems of neighbouring peoples.
examples.cn: 民族学比较相邻各民族的亲属制度。

examples.en: He teaches ethnology in a museum studies programme.
examples.cn: 他在一个博物馆研究项目中教授民族学。

examples.en: The library keeps a full run of the journal of ethnology.
examples.cn: 图书馆保存着这份民族学期刊的完整过刊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ethno 民族 + logy 学问」——研究各民族的学问；这只是拆词联想，与严格的词源考证并不等同。

root: 希腊语 ethnos（民族、族群）+ logos（论说、道理）→ -logia（某类研究）→ 新拉丁语 ethnologia → 英语 ethnology，核心义「对各民族作有理据的比较研究」。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers the whole comparative discipline, then the older programme of origins and distribution, then the accumulated knowledge of one people or region.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指整门比较性的学科，再指较早的起源与分布研究纲领，最后指关于某一民族或地区积累起来的知识。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many peoples laid side by side on one long table for comparison.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多民族被并排摆在一张长桌上作比较。

branches.en: The comparative discipline is the central sense of the word.
branches.cn: 比较性的学科是这个词的核心义项。

branches.en: Classifying peoples by origin is the historical programme inside the discipline.
branches.cn: 按起源给民族分类，是这门学科内部的历史纲领。

branches.en: Knowledge of one region is the discipline applied to a single object.
branches.cn: 关于某一地区的知识，是这门学科落到单一对象上的用法。

branches.en: Comparison and classification used to be two names for one task.
branches.cn: 比较与分类一度是同一件事的两个名字。

branches.en: Origins are argued from regional knowledge, and regional knowledge is organised by origin.
branches.cn: 起源问题靠区域知识来论证，区域知识又按起源来组织。

intro.en: Ethnology is a Greek compound: ethnos, a people, plus -logy from logos, reasoned account.
intro.cn: ethnology 是希腊语复合词：ethnos（民族）加 -logy（源自 logos，有理据的论说）。

latinIntro.en: New Latin ethnologia fixed the shape of the word before English borrowed it.
latinIntro.cn: 新拉丁语 ethnologia 在英语借入之前就固定了这个词的词形。

items.example: Ethnos is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: ethnos 是这个复合词的前半部分。

items.example: Logos gives the reasoning half of the word.
items.exampleCN: logos 提供这个词「论说」的那一半。

items.meaning: a field of study or discourse
items.meaningCN: 表示某类研究或论述的后缀
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -logia 用来命名整门学科。

items.example: The prefix ethno- also builds ethnography.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ethno- 也构成 ethnography。

items.example: Ethnologia is the learned Latin form.
items.exampleCN: ethnologia 是学术拉丁语形式。

items.meaningCN: 由名词构成形容词的后缀

items.example: Ethnological collections are grouped by region.
items.exampleCN: 民族学藏品按地区分组。

items.meaningCN: 表示「从事某事的人」的后缀

latinEntries.meaning: relating to the study of peoples

definition_zh: 悦耳的；动听的；音调优美的
definition_en: pleasing to the ear, especially because of the smooth and pleasant sound of words, a voice, or a melody
core_image: 一句念出口就顺着耳朵滑过去的话，音节像水一样连成弧线
scene: 音乐厅的排练间隙，小提琴手为新曲挑了一个念起来顺口的标题。The violinist chose a euphonious title for the new sonata.
sceneCN: 这里 euphonious 是「念起来好听的」（第 2 个义项：词或名字的读音悦耳）；句意：小提琴手为新奏鸣曲挑了一个读音悦耳的标题。

pos.zh: 悦耳的；动听的；音调优美的

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语 eu-（好）与 phōnē（声音）构成，义为「谐音；悦耳的音调」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「悦耳地；动听地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「悦耳；音调的优美」

senses.title: Pleasing to the ear
senses.definition: giving pleasure to the ear, said of any sound that is smooth rather than harsh
senses.definitionCN: 任何听起来顺滑而不刺耳、令人愉悦的声音
senses.example: The euphonious chime of the temple bells drifted across the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 寺庙钟声悦耳，飘过山谷。
senses.why: Greek eu- means well or good and phōnē means voice or sound, so the adjective first says that a sound is well-sounding, judged by the ear alone.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 eu- 意为「好」，phōnē 意为「声音」，所以这个词最初就是说某个声音「发声得好」，只凭耳朵判断。

senses.title: Pleasant to pronounce
senses.definition: of a word, name, or phrase, having a smooth sequence of sounds that is easy and pleasant to say
senses.definitionCN: 指单词、名字或短语的音节组合顺滑，念起来轻松好听
senses.example: The village name sounds euphonious to most visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 在多数来访者听来，这个村子的名字很好听。
senses.why: A word is a stretch of sound as well as a unit of meaning, and this adjective can judge only the sound shape, leaving what the word means out of account.
senses.whyCN: 一个词既是意义的单位，也是一段声音；这个词可以只评判声音的形状，把词义放在一边。

senses.title: Sweet in tone
senses.definition: of a voice or an instrument, having a warm and smooth tone that is pleasant to listen to
senses.definitionCN: 指人声或乐器的音色温暖圆润，听起来舒服
senses.example: Her euphonious alto filled the small chapel without effort.
senses.exampleCN: 她柔美的女低音毫不费力地填满了小教堂。
senses.why: Phōnē covers any voiced sound, so when the adjective moves from speech to singing it keeps the same judgement of tone.
senses.whyCN: phōnē 涵盖一切发出的声音，所以这个词从说话转到歌唱时，仍然是对音色的同一种评价。

senses.title: Smooth in rhythm
senses.definition: of prose or verse, having a rhythm and a sequence of sounds that reads aloud gracefully
senses.definitionCN: 指散文或诗歌的节奏与音响顺序朗读起来流畅优雅
senses.example: The essay is euphonious without ever becoming merely decorative.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章音律流畅，却从不流于纯粹的装饰。
senses.why: Prose read aloud is also sound, so a sentence whose stresses fall pleasantly earns the same word that a voice or a melody earns.
senses.whyCN: 朗读出来的散文也是声音，所以重音落得舒服的句子，会得到与嗓音、旋律相同的这个词。

intro.en: Euphonious is built from three Greek pieces, eu-, phōnē, and the adjective ending -ous, and its family came into English through the noun euphony.
intro.cn: euphonious 由三个希腊语构件搭成：eu-、phōnē 与形容词词尾 -ous；这一词族是经名词 euphony 进入英语的。

items.en: Eu- is a prefix of approval, meaning well, good, or easily.
items.cn: eu- 是表示赞许的前缀，意为「好、善、容易」。

items.en: Phōnē means voice or sound, and it also gives phone and phonetics.
items.cn: phōnē 意为嗓音、声音，也是 phone 与 phonetics 的来源。

items.en: Euphōnia, sweetness of voice, and the adjective euphōnos, sweet-voiced, are both recorded in Greek.
items.cn: 希腊语有 euphōnia「嗓音的甜美」与形容词 euphōnos「嗓音甜美的」。

items.en: Late Latin took euphonia as a noun of pleasant sound, keeping the Greek shape almost unchanged.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语借入 euphonia，指悦耳的声音，几乎原样保留了希腊语的形式。

items.en: English coined euphony first, then added -ous to make euphonious in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 英语先有 euphony，十八世纪再加 -ous 构成 euphonious。

items.en: Modern use extends the adjective to names, instruments, and prose rhythm.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个形容词扩展到名字、乐器与散文节奏上。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same Greek sound root; the near-meaning group gathers other words for sweet sound.
note.cn: 形近组收同一希腊语「声音」词根构成的词；近义组收其他表示声音甜美的词。

entries.definition: the noun for pleasantness of sound, the base from which the adjective was formed
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「谐音、悦耳的音调」，形容词正是由它构成。

entries.definition: an adjective meaning the same as euphonious but shorter and less common
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「悦耳的」，与 euphonious 同义，但更短也更少用。

entries.definition: a brass instrument named for its sweet sound, not a word for the quality itself
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「上低音号」，因音色甜美而得名，并非表示音质本身的词。

entries.definition: having a tune that is pleasant to hear, said especially of music and birdsong
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「旋律优美的」，多用于音乐与鸟鸣。

entries.definition: sweet and flowing in sound, often of a voice or of speech that pleases almost too much
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「声音甜美流畅的」，多形容嗓音或言语，有时带「甜得过分」的意味。

entries.definition: deep, full, and resonant, a quality of sound rather than of word shape
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「声音浑厚响亮的」，说的是音色而非词形。

normalIntro.en: These hooks pull the word apart into the Greek pieces it is actually made of.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子把词拆成它真正由之构成的希腊语构件。

normal.en: Eu- says good and phōnē says sound: euphonious is literally well-sounding.
normal.cn: eu- 是「好」，phōnē 是「声音」：euphonious 字面上就是「发声得好」。

normal.en: The noun euphony is shorter; the adjective adds -ous to describe the quality.
normal.cn: 名词 euphony 更短，形容词加 -ous 来描述这种性质。

normal.en: Phone and phonetics share the same phōnē, so the sound root links all three.
normal.cn: phone 与 phonetics 共用同一个 phōnē，声音词根把三者连在一起。

normal.en: A euphonious name is chosen for how it sounds, not for what it means.
normal.cn: euphonious name 是按其读音、而不是按其含义挑出来的名字。

normal.en: Compare melodious: melodious is about tune, euphonious is about the sound of words and voices.
normal.cn: 对比 melodious：melodious 说的是旋律，euphonious 说的是词句与嗓音的音响。

abstract.en: Picture a bell struck once in a still valley, the note spreading in a clean smooth ring.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的山谷里敲一下钟，音波以干净平滑的圆环散开。

abstract.en: Picture a name written on a card and then spoken aloud, the syllables sliding into each other without a bump.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字写在卡片上，再被念出声，音节彼此滑接，毫无磕碰。

abstract.en: Picture a singer holding one long note at the back of a chapel, the tone warm and round.
abstract.cn: 想象歌者在教堂后部拖住一个长音，音色温暖圆润。

examples.en: The euphonious names of the villages made the map pleasant to read aloud.
examples.cn: 这些村子悦耳的名字让地图念起来很舒服。

examples.en: Critics praised the euphonious rhythm of the closing lines.
examples.cn: 评论家称赞结尾几行的音律流畅。

examples.en: Few sounds are more euphonious than rain on a tin roof at night.
examples.cn: 很少有声音比夜里雨打铁皮屋顶更悦耳。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优 · 否尼厄斯」——谐音像「优美的声音」，只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 eu-（好）＋ phōnē（声音、嗓音）＋ 形容词词尾 -ous → 希腊语 euphōnos（嗓音甜美）与 euphōnia（声音甜美）→ 晚期拉丁语 euphonia → 英语 euphony → euphonious；核心义「声音本身好」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses apply one judgement, well-sounding, to a general sound, then to a word or name, to a voice, and to the rhythm of prose.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项把同一个判断「发声得好」依次用在一般声音、词或名字、嗓音，以及散文的节奏上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single note struck in a quiet valley, spreading in a smooth unbroken ring.
core.cn: 核心意象：安静山谷里敲响的一个音，以平滑不断的圆环散开。

branches.en: THE EAR: any smooth sound earns the adjective in its most general use.
branches.cn: 耳朵线：任何平滑的声音都能得到这个形容词，这是最一般的用法。

branches.en: THE WORD: a name is judged by its syllables rather than by its sense.
branches.cn: 词形线：名字由音节来评判，而不是由含义。

branches.en: THE VOICE: a warm tone extends the judgement to singing.
branches.cn: 嗓音线：温暖的音色把这一判断延伸到歌唱。

branches.en: THE PAGE: prose read aloud is sound too, so its rhythm can be euphonious.
branches.cn: 书页线：朗读的散文也是声音，所以它的节奏也能悦耳。

branches.en: A sound and a word are both stretches of audible material.
branches.cn: 声音与词都是一段可听见的材料。

intro.en: Euphonious is a Greek compound with a Latin-shaped adjective ending; its pieces are eu-, phōnē, and -ous.
intro.cn: euphonious 是希腊语复合词加上拉丁语形态的形容词词尾：构件是 eu-、phōnē 与 -ous。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed euphonia from Greek as a noun of sweet sound, and the adjective ending -ous reached English through Old French from Latin -osus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借入 euphonia，指悦耳的声音；形容词词尾 -ous 经由古法语来自拉丁语 -osus。

items.example: Eu- marks approval in many learned words.
items.exampleCN: eu- 在许多学术词里表示赞许。

items.example: Phōnē is the sound root of the family.
items.exampleCN: phōnē 是这一词族的「声音」词根。

items.meaning: a sound, or a device for sound
items.example: Phone is a direct borrowing of phōnē.
items.exampleCN: phone 是 phōnē 的直接借用。

items.example: Euphony came into English before the adjective.
items.exampleCN: euphony 比形容词更早进入英语。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous turns a noun of sound into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 把表示声音的名词变成形容词。

items.example: It carries the -ous ending into euphonious.
items.exampleCN: 它把 -ous 词尾带进 euphonious。

items.example: Euphonious describes the sound, not the meaning.
items.exampleCN: euphonious 描述的是声音，不是意义。

items.meaning: in a pleasing way to the ear
items.example: The adverb describes how something sounds.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词描述某物听起来怎样。

latinEntries.example: Euphonia is the Latin form behind euphony.
latinEntries.exampleCN: euphonia 是 euphony 背后的拉丁语形式。
拉丁语 -osus 变成英语的 -ous。

definition_zh: 疏散；撤离；排空；排泄
definition_en: to move people away from a dangerous place, or to empty a container, a space, or the body of what is inside it
core_image: 一队人拎着行李走出空荡的楼，门在身后关上，屋里只剩下回声
scene: 洪水漫过街道，救援队挨家敲门，把居民送到高处。Rescue teams helped evacuate the whole street before the river rose further.
sceneCN: 这里 evacuate 是「疏散人员」（第 1 个义项：把人从危险的地方转移出去）；句意：救援队赶在河水继续上涨前帮助疏散了整条街的人。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「疏散；撤离；排空」
由本词加 -ee（受动作影响的人）构成，义为「被疏散者」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「促排泄的；用于排空的」

senses.title: To move people out of danger
senses.definition: to move people away from a place where they are in danger, usually in an organised way
senses.definitionCN: 通常有组织地把人从有危险的地方转移出去
senses.example: Fire officers evacuated the hotel within ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 消防人员在十分钟内疏散了旅馆里的人。
senses.why: Latin e- or ex- means out and vacuus means empty: to evacuate is to make a place empty of its people, and the danger is the reason for emptying it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 e- 与 ex- 意为「出」，vacuus 意为「空」：evacuate 就是让一个地方在人这方面变空，危险则是把地方腾空的理由。

senses.title: To leave a place
senses.definition: of people, troops, or an organisation, to leave a place that is being given up or is no longer safe
senses.definitionCN: 指人员、部队或机构离开一个被放弃或已不安全的地方
senses.example: The staff evacuated the office when the alarm sounded.
senses.exampleCN: 警报响起时，员工撤离了办公室。
senses.why: Once the place is emptied, the people who leave are the ones doing the emptying, so the subject of the verb shifts from the building to the people.
senses.whyCN: 地方一旦被腾空，离开的人就成了执行腾空的一方，于是动词的主语从建筑物转到了人身上。

senses.title: To empty a container or space
senses.definition: to remove the contents of a container, a vessel, or an enclosed space, leaving it empty
senses.definitionCN: 把容器、管道或封闭空间中的东西取出，使其变空
senses.example: Engineers evacuated the tank before the inspection.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在检查前把罐体排空了。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most literal use of the Latin verb, which simply meant to make something empty, with no danger involved at all.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语动词最古老、最字面的用法，意思只是「使某物变空」，完全不含危险的意思。

senses.title: To discharge waste from the body
senses.definition: to pass waste matter out of the bowels or another part of the body, a medical and formal use
senses.definitionCN: 把废物从肠道或身体其他部位排出，属医学与正式用法
senses.example: The patient had not evacuated the bowels for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 病人已经三天没有排便了。
senses.why: Latin medical writers used evacuare for clearing the body of humours and waste, so the emptying image was applied to the inside of the body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁医学作者用 evacuare 表示把体液与废物从体内清出，于是「腾空」的意象被用到了身体内部。

senses.title: To remove air or gas
senses.definition: in technical use, to draw air or gas out of a sealed space so that a vacuum is left
senses.definitionCN: 技术用语，把空气或气体从密闭空间中抽出，留下真空
senses.example: The chamber is evacuated before the samples are sealed in.
senses.exampleCN: 样品密封进去之前，腔体要先抽真空。
senses.why: A sealed space is a container, and its contents happen to be gas, so taking the gas out is emptying it in the most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 密闭空间就是一个容器，只是里面装的东西恰好是气体，把气体取出来，正是最字面意义上的「腾空」。

intro.en: Evacuate comes straight from Latin evacuare, built on vacuus, empty, and the prefix e- or ex-, out.
intro.cn: evacuate 直接来自拉丁语 evacuare，由 vacuus「空的」与前缀 e- 或 ex-「出」构成。

items.en: Vacuus means empty or free of occupants, and it also gives vacuum and vacant.
items.cn: vacuus 意为空的、无人占用的，也是 vacuum 与 vacant 的来源。

items.en: The verb vacare means to be empty or to be free of something.
items.cn: 动词 vacare 意为空着、没有被占用。

items.en: Ex plus vacuus formed evacuare, to empty out, with the past participle evacuatus.
items.cn: ex 与 vacuus 构成 evacuare，意为「把……腾空」，过去分词是 evacuatus。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the sixteenth century first for clearing the body and emptying vessels.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个词，最初用于清空身体与排空器皿。

items.en: Military use added the sense of withdrawing troops from a place, and the civilian sense of moving people out followed.
items.cn: 军事用法增加了「把部队撤出某地」的意思，随后又有了转移平民的用法。

items.en: Modern disaster language made evacuate a household word for moving people out of floods, fires, and storms.
items.cn: 现代灾害语言让 evacuate 成为「把人们撤出洪水、火灾与风暴」的常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the vacuus family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of leaving and emptying.
note.cn: 形近组收 vacuus 这一词族；近义组收表示离开与腾空的动词。

entries.definition: the act of moving people out or emptying a space, formed with -ion
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「疏散、撤离、排空」，由动词加 -ion 构成。

entries.definition: a person who has been moved out of a dangerous place, formed with -ee
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「被疏散者」，由动词加 -ee 构成。

entries.definition: a space with nothing in it, from the same Latin word for empty
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「真空、空白」，来自同一个表示「空」的拉丁词。

entries.definition: to pull back troops or people from a place, stressing a deliberate retreat
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「撤出、撤退」，强调有意的后撤。

entries.definition: to take everything out of a container, with no suggestion of danger
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「倒空、腾空」，不含危险的意味。

entries.definition: to leave a place or a person behind for good, with a stronger sense of desertion
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「弃置、抛下」，带有更强的遗弃意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin pieces of the word and the phrases the verb really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用这个词的拉丁语构件，以及它真正出现的搭配。

normal.en: E- is out and vacuus is empty: to evacuate is to empty a place out.
normal.cn: e- 是「出」，vacuus 是「空」：evacuate 就是把一个地方腾空。

normal.en: Vacuum, vacant, and vacate share the same empty root.
normal.cn: vacuum、vacant 与 vacate 共用同一个表示「空」的词根。

normal.en: You evacuate a building, but you also evacuate your bowels: both are emptying.
normal.cn: evacuate 可以接 building，也可以接 bowels：两者都是「腾空」。

normal.en: The passive is common: residents were evacuated to safety.
normal.cn: 被动式很常见：居民被转移到安全地带。

normal.en: Compare empty: empty is neutral, while evacuate usually implies a threat or an order.
normal.cn: 对比 empty：empty 是中性的，而 evacuate 通常暗示威胁或命令。

abstract.en: Picture a line of people carrying bags out of a lit doorway, a warden counting them as they pass.
abstract.cn: 想象一队人拎着包从亮着的门口出来，引导员在门口清点人数。

abstract.en: Picture an empty office with the lights still on and a cup of tea going cold on the desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一间空掉的办公室，灯还亮着，桌上的茶正在变凉。

abstract.en: Picture a tank with its valve open, the last of the liquid running out and the metal ringing hollow.
abstract.cn: 想象一只打开阀门的罐子，最后的液体流尽，金属敲起来发出空响。

examples.en: Police evacuated the market after the gas leak was reported.
examples.cn: 接到燃气泄漏的报告后，警方疏散了市场里的人。

examples.en: The whole village was evacuated before the dam broke.
examples.cn: 大坝决口前，整个村子的人都被疏散了。

examples.en: Nurses evacuated the ward quietly, moving patients to the lower floor.
examples.cn: 护士们安静地撤离了病房，把病人转移到楼下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一挖空」——evacuate 读起来像「一挖空」：房间挖空、街道撤空；纯属谐音拆词联想，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 e- 与 ex-（出）＋ vacuus（空的）→ evacuare（把……腾空，过去分词 evacuatus）→ 英语 evacuate；核心义「使变空」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses all empty something out: a dangerous place of its people, a place of its occupants, a container of its contents, the body of its waste, and a sealed chamber of its air.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都在把某样东西腾空：危险之地的人、被放弃之地的占用者、容器的内容物、身体的废物，以及密闭腔体里的空气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of people leaving a building that stands empty behind them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人走出身后的空楼。

branches.en: THE ALARM: making a dangerous place empty of people is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 警报线：让危险之地在人这方面变空，是日常义项。

branches.en: THE DEPARTURE: the people who empty the place are seen leaving it.
branches.cn: 离开线：执行腾空的人被看作离开的人。

branches.en: THE VESSEL: emptying a container is the oldest and most literal use.
branches.cn: 容器线：排空容器是最古老、最字面的用法。

branches.en: THE BODY AND THE CHAMBER: waste and gas are just contents to be taken out.
branches.cn: 身体与腔体线：废物和气体不过是需要取出的内容物。

branches.en: All three keep one frame: a space is made empty, whether by people leaving or by contents being removed.
branches.cn: 三个义项共用同一个框架：空间被腾空，或靠人离开，或靠内容物被取走。

intro.en: Evacuate joins a Latin prefix of exit to a Latin adjective of emptiness, and English adds the verb ending -ate.
intro.cn: evacuate 把表示「出」的拉丁语前缀接到表示「空」的拉丁语形容词上，英语再加上动词词尾 -ate。

latinIntro.en: Latin vacuus, vacare, and evacuare are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root behind vacuus is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vacuus、vacare 与 evacuare 都有文献记录，只有 vacuus 背后更早的印欧词根不确定。

items.example: The prefix marks the movement outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出向外的动作。

items.example: Vacuus is the adjective of emptiness.
items.exampleCN: vacuus 是表示「空」的形容词。

items.meaning: to be empty, to be free
items.example: Vacare is the verb behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: vacare 是这个形容词背后的动词。

items.example: The prefix and the adjective made this verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与形容词合成了这个动词。

items.example: It forms evacuate from the Latin participle.
items.exampleCN: 它由拉丁语分词构成 evacuate。

items.meaning: a space with nothing in it
items.example: Vacuum keeps the Latin neuter form.
items.exampleCN: vacuum 保留了拉丁语的中性形式。

items.example: Vacant keeps the same empty root.
items.exampleCN: vacant 保留同一个表示「空」的词根。

items.meaning: the act of emptying or moving people out

latinEntries.example: Vacuus is the source of vacuum.
latinEntries.exampleCN: vacuus 是 vacuum 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Vacare gives the verb family its shape.
latinEntries.exampleCN: vacare 给这一动词族定下形态。

latinEntries.example: Evacuare is the direct source of the word.
latinEntries.exampleCN: evacuare 是这个词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 评估；评价；估算
definition_en: to judge the quality, value or importance of something
core_image: 把一件东西放上天平，仔细衡量它的分量
scene: 面试结束后，评委开始评估每位候选人的表现。After the interviews, the judges began to evaluate each candidate's performance.
sceneCN: 这里 evaluate 是「评估」（第 1 个义项：判断质量、价值或重要性）；句意：面试结束后，评委开始评估每位候选人的表现。

senses.title: Judge quality or value
senses.definition: to judge how good, useful or important something is
senses.definitionCN: 判断某事物有多好、多有用或多重要
senses.example: Teachers evaluate students' progress each term.
senses.exampleCN: 老师每学期评估学生的进步。
senses.why: The word contains value, so evaluating is putting a value on something.
senses.whyCN: 这个词包含 value，因此 evaluate 就是给事物定出价值。

senses.title: Work out an amount
senses.definition: to calculate the amount or effect of something
senses.definitionCN: 计算某事物的数量或影响
senses.example: Engineers evaluated the cost of the repair.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师估算了维修成本。
senses.why: Judging value and calculating cost both weigh something against a standard.
senses.whyCN: 判断价值与计算成本，都是把事物放在标准上衡量。

intro.en: Evaluate comes from French évaluer, to find the value of, from value.
intro.cn: evaluate 源自法语 évaluer（确定价值），来自 value。

items.en: Valere means to be worth or be strong.
items.cn: valere 意为有价值或强健。

items.en: Value means worth.
items.cn: value 意为价值。

items.en: Évaluer means to work out the value.
items.cn: évaluer 意为算出价值。

items.en: Evaluate enters English with the same sense.
items.cn: evaluate 以相同含义进入英语。

items.en: It covers performance, risk and cost.
items.cn: 它涵盖表现、风险与成本。

note.en: Evaluate is close to assess and judge, with value at its core.
note.cn: evaluate 与评估、判断相近，核心是价值。

entries.definition: the act of judging
judging value
worth
to judge the quality of something
to form an opinion about something
to give a value to something

normalIntro.en: Evaluate puts a value on something, like a price tag on a skill.
normalIntro.cn: evaluate 就是给事物标上价值，像给技能贴上价签。

normal.en: Evaluate performance means judge how well someone did.
normal.cn: evaluate performance 意为判断某人做得如何。

normal.en: Evaluate the risk means work out how dangerous it is.
normal.cn: evaluate the risk 意为算出风险有多大。

normal.en: Carefully evaluate means do not decide too quickly.
normal.cn: carefully evaluate 意为不要过快下结论。

normal.en: The noun evaluation names the judging process.
normal.cn: 名词 evaluation 指评估过程。

normal.en: Compare assess: assess is broader, evaluate stresses value.
normal.cn: 对比 assess：assess 更宽泛，evaluate 强调价值。

abstract.en: Picture an object placed on a balance.
abstract.cn: 想象一件物品被放上天平。

abstract.en: Imagine a scorecard filled in row by row.
abstract.cn: 想象一张评分表被一行行填满。

abstract.en: Think of a jeweler holding a stone up to the light.
abstract.cn: 想象珠宝商把宝石举到光下细看。

examples.en: The committee will evaluate all the proposals.
examples.cn: 委员会将评估所有提案。

examples.en: We need to evaluate the risks before we start.
examples.cn: 开始之前我们需要评估风险。

examples.en: It is hard to evaluate a book by its cover.
examples.cn: 仅凭封面很难评价一本书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）＋ value（价值）＋ ate」——把价值算出来，就是评估；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 valere（有价值）→ 法语 value（价值）→ évaluer（估价）→ evaluate，核心义「衡量并定出价值」。

sensesIntro.en: Evaluate first judges quality or worth, and then works out an amount or effect.
sensesIntro.cn: evaluate 先判断质量或价值，再计算数量或影响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object weighed on a balance.
core.cn: 核心意象：放在天平上称量的物品。

branches.en: Judging quality is the main sense.
branches.cn: 判断质量是主要义项。

branches.en: Calculating an amount is evaluation with numbers.
branches.cn: 计算数量是用数字进行评估。

branches.en: Both quality and cost are weighed against a standard.
branches.cn: 质量与成本都要对照标准衡量。

branches.en: Teachers evaluate, committees evaluate, readers evaluate.
branches.cn: 老师、委员会与读者都会评估。

branches.en: Risk and cost are common evaluated quantities.
branches.cn: 风险与成本是常见的被估量。

intro.en: Evaluate is built on value, with the verb ending -ate.
intro.cn: evaluate 建立在 value 之上，带动词词尾 -ate。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere, to be worth, gives value and evaluate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 valere（有价值）衍生出 value 与 evaluate。

items.example: French évaluer is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 法语 évaluer 是直接来源。
evaluative 描述评价性的评论。

definition_zh: 评估；评价；评估报告
definition_en: the process of judging the quality or value of something
core_image: 一份写满分数与评语的表格，被郑重地交到手上
scene: 学期末，学校会对每位老师进行一次正式评估。At the end of the term, the school carries out a formal evaluation of each teacher.
sceneCN: 这里 evaluation 是「评估」（第 1 个义项：判断质量或价值的过程）；句意：学期末，学校会对每位老师进行一次正式评估。

senses.title: The judging process
senses.definition: the process of judging how good or useful something is
senses.definitionCN: 判断某事物有多好或多有用的过程
senses.example: The project is still under evaluation.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目仍在评估中。
senses.why: The noun names the action behind the verb evaluate.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指动词 evaluate 背后的行为。

senses.title: A written judgment
senses.definition: a report that gives a judgment about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物作出判断的报告
senses.example: The evaluation praised her teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 评估报告称赞了她的教学。
senses.why: The result of evaluating is often written down as a report.
senses.whyCN: 评估的结果常常被写成报告。

intro.en: Evaluation adds -ion to evaluate, from French évaluer and value.
intro.cn: evaluation 在 evaluate 后加 -ion，源自法语 évaluer 与 value。

items.en: Valere means to be worth.
items.cn: valere 意为有价值。

items.en: Évaluer means to work out value.
items.cn: évaluer 意为算出价值。

items.en: Evaluate enters English as a verb.
items.cn: evaluate 作为动词进入英语。

items.en: Evaluation names the judging process.
items.cn: evaluation 指评估过程。

items.en: It also names the written report.
items.cn: 它也指书面报告。

note.en: Evaluation is the noun of evaluate, close to assessment and review.
note.cn: evaluation 是 evaluate 的名词，与评定、审查相近。

entries.definition: to judge value
judging value
someone who evaluates
a judgment about quality
a careful examination of something
a judgment of value or performance

normalIntro.en: An evaluation is the scorecard after the judging is done.
normalIntro.cn: evaluation 就是评判结束后留下的评分表。

normal.en: A formal evaluation follows official rules.
normal.cn: formal evaluation 按正式规则进行。

normal.en: Performance evaluation judges how well someone works.
normal.cn: performance evaluation 评判某人的工作表现。

normal.en: Carry out an evaluation means do the judging.
normal.cn: carry out an evaluation 意为开展评估。

normal.en: Evaluation criteria are the standards used.
normal.cn: evaluation criteria 是所采用的标准。

normal.en: Compare assessment: assessment is often broader, evaluation stresses value.
normal.cn: 对比 assessment：assessment 往往更宽泛，evaluation 强调价值。

abstract.en: Picture a form with boxes for scores and comments.
abstract.cn: 想象一张有分数栏和评语栏的表格。

abstract.en: Imagine a seal pressed onto a finished report.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章盖在完成的报告上。

abstract.en: Think of a scale that has just come to rest.
abstract.cn: 想象天平刚刚静止下来。

examples.en: The new policy is under evaluation.
examples.cn: 新政策正在评估之中。

examples.en: We received a positive evaluation from the inspector.
examples.cn: 我们收到了检查员的正面评价。

examples.en: The evaluation of the course takes several weeks.
examples.cn: 对这门课的评估需要数周。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「evaluate（评估）＋ ion」——评估之后留下的那份判断，就是评估报告；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 valere（有价值）→ 法语 value → evaluate（评估）＋ -ion → evaluation，核心义「衡量价值的过程与结果」。

sensesIntro.en: Evaluation first names the judging process, and then the written report that records it.
sensesIntro.cn: evaluation 先指评估过程，再指记录该过程的书面报告。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scorecard with marks and written comments.
core.cn: 核心意象：写有分数与评语的评分表。

branches.en: The process of judging is the first sense.
branches.cn: 判断的过程是首要义项。

branches.en: The written judgment is the second sense.
branches.cn: 书面判断是第二个义项。

branches.en: A report records what the process found.
branches.cn: 报告记录了过程所得。

branches.en: Criteria make evaluation fair and repeatable.
branches.cn: 标准让评估公平且可重复。

branches.en: A good evaluation explains its reasons.
branches.cn: 好的评估报告会说明理由。

intro.en: Evaluation adds the noun suffix -ion to evaluate.
intro.cn: evaluation 在 evaluate 后加名词后缀 -ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere, to be worth, is the root of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 valere（有价值）是整个词族的根。

definition_zh: 蒸发；使蒸发；消失；使浓缩
definition_en: to change from a liquid into vapor, or to cause a liquid to do so; also to disappear gradually
core_image: 太阳照在湿石板上，水膜先变薄，随后整片湿痕无声地退去
scene: 太阳升高后，草叶上的露水一点点变少。 By mid-morning the dew has begun to evaporate from the warm grass.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「液体受热后变成水汽而减少」（第 1 个义项：液体汽化）；句意为到了半上午，露水已在温暖的草地上开始蒸发。

senses.title: Turn from liquid to vapor
senses.definition: to change from a liquid into vapor, usually at the surface and below boiling point
senses.definitionCN: 液体在表面、低于沸点时变成水汽
senses.example: Rainwater evaporates from the roof soon after the shower passes.
senses.exampleCN: 阵雨过后，屋面上的雨水很快就蒸发。
senses.why: The verb profiles the change of state itself, not the resulting loss or the tool used.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词凸出状态变化本身，而不是由此造成的损失或所借助的工具。

senses.title: Dry up completely
senses.definition: of a liquid, to disappear entirely by evaporation
senses.definitionCN: （液体）因蒸发而完全消失
senses.example: The pool evaporates in summer, leaving cracked mud.
senses.exampleCN: 这水塘在夏天干涸，留下龟裂的泥。
senses.why: When the last liquid is gone, the verb shifts from the process to its end point.
senses.whyCN: 当最后的液体消失，词义就从过程转到终点。

senses.title: Remove moisture by heating
senses.definition: to drive water or another solvent off by heating
senses.definitionCN: 加热把水或溶剂蒸掉
senses.example: The laboratory evaporates the solution to recover the salt.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把溶液蒸干以回收盐。
senses.why: The transitive use makes evaporation an action performed on a material by someone.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法把蒸发变成某人施加于材料的动作。

senses.title: Concentrate a solution
senses.definition: to make a solution more concentrated by removing part of its solvent
senses.definitionCN: 除去部分溶剂，使溶液变浓
senses.example: Slow heating evaporates the broth until it thickens.
senses.exampleCN: 缓慢加热让汤汁蒸发，直到变稠。
senses.why: The purpose shifts from removing water to keeping what remains, which is the culinary and chemical use.
senses.whyCN: 目的从「除去水」转到「留下其余成分」，这是烹饪与化学的用法。

senses.title: Vanish figuratively
senses.definition: to disappear gradually, especially money, hopes or support
senses.definitionCN: （钱、希望、支持）逐渐消失
senses.example: The grant evaporated after the second review.
senses.exampleCN: 第二次评审之后，这笔资助就化为乌有。
senses.why: An abstract quantity is imagined as a volatile liquid that leaves no residue.
senses.whyCN: 抽象之物被想象成一种挥发后不留残渣的液体。

senses.title: Fade in intensity
senses.definition: to become weaker or less intense, as if dissipating
senses.definitionCN: （情绪、紧张等）逐渐减弱
senses.example: The crowd's anger evaporated once the referee explained.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判一解释，人群的怒气就消散了。
senses.why: Intensity is treated as a quantity that can be lost to the air, like heat or moisture.
senses.whyCN: 强度被当作像热量或水分那样会散失到空气中的量。

senses.title: Be lost from soil or plants
senses.definition: of water, to be lost from soil, leaves or other surfaces into the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: （水）从土壤、叶片等表面散失到大气
senses.example: Moisture evaporates quickly from bare, compacted soil.
senses.exampleCN: 裸露板结的土壤里，水分蒸发得很快。
senses.why: This is the passive side of the water cycle: the water is not acting, it is simply leaving.
senses.whyCN: 这是水循环的被动一面：水并没有主动做什么，只是离开了。

senses.title: Emit vapor (archaic)
senses.definition: of a substance, to give off vapor or steam
senses.definitionCN: （物质）散发出水汽或蒸汽
senses.example: Early chemistry texts say that heated salts evaporate a sharp vapor.
senses.exampleCN: 早期化学文献说，受热的盐会散出刺鼻的水汽。
senses.why: The old sense focuses on what comes out of the substance rather than on the substance changing state.
senses.whyCN: 旧义关注从物质里出来的东西，而不是物质本身的状态变化。

intro.en: The Latin and French stages are well documented, while the deeper origin of vapor and the exact date of the figurative sense are less certain.
intro.cn: 拉丁与法语阶段有较清楚的文献记录；vapor 的更深来源、以及比喻义的确切首见年代则不够确定。

items.en: Evaporare is built from e- 'out of' and vaporare 'to steam', itself from vapor 'steam, vapor'. The image is steam leaving a liquid.
items.cn: evaporare 由 e-「向外」与 vaporare「冒汽」构成，后者又来自 vapor「蒸汽、水汽」。意象是蒸汽离开液体。

items.en: The verb is attested in Late Latin technical writing. Its noun evaporatio supplies the action noun used in modern science.
items.cn: 该动词见于晚期拉丁语的技术文献。其名词 evaporatio 提供了现代科学使用的动作名词。

items.en: Middle French évaporer passed the verb to English. The earliest English examples concern moisture leaving a body or a liquid.
items.cn: 中古法语 évaporer 把该动词传入英语。最早的英语例子讲的是湿气离开物体或液体。

items.en: Chemistry gave the transitive use 'to drive off a solvent by heat', which remains the laboratory sense today.
items.cn: 化学带来了「加热驱除溶剂」的及物用法，这一直是今天的实验室义。

items.en: The figurative sense for hopes, funds or anger is relatively recent. It is generally treated as an extension of the physical image, but the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 用于希望、资金或怒气的比喻义出现较晚。一般认为它是物理意象的延伸，但确切首见年代存疑。

note.en: The first group looks and sounds like evaporate but comes from other roots; the second group describes the same change, its result, or its reverse.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上像 evaporate，但词源不同；第二组描述同一变化、其结果或相反过程。

entries.definition: to move people out of a place. It comes from Latin vacuus 'empty', so the image is emptying a space, not vaporizing a liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 疏散；撤离。来自拉丁语 vacuus「空的」，意象是把空间腾空，而不是液体汽化。

entries.definition: to judge value or quality, from Latin valere 'to be worth'. The similarity is only in the opening syllables.
entries.definitionCN: 评估；评价。来自拉丁语 valere「有价值」，相似只在前几个音节。

entries.definition: to show clearly, from Latin vincere 'to conquer'. It has nothing to do with vapor.
entries.definitionCN: 表明；显示。来自拉丁语 vincere「征服」，与水汽无关。

entries.definition: to turn into vapor by any means, including boiling; evaporate is the slower surface process.
entries.definitionCN: 汽化。以任何方式变成水汽，包括沸腾；evaporate 指较慢的表面过程。

entries.definition: to become completely dry, focusing on the end state rather than the mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 干涸；枯竭。强调最终状态，而不是机制。

entries.definition: the neutral word for going out of sight; the figurative use of evaporate adds the image of volatile loss.
entries.definitionCN: 消失。中性的「看不见了」；evaporate 的比喻义多出「挥发式损失」的意象。

entries.definition: to become weaker or less vivid, often of color, sound or feeling; it stresses diminishing intensity rather than loss of substance.
entries.definitionCN: 褪去；减弱。多指颜色、声音或情绪变淡，强调强度下降而不是物质消失。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'out' and the base means 'steam', so the verb is 'steam out'.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「向外」，基础词意为「蒸汽」，动词就是「向外冒汽」。

normal.en: The family runs evaporation, evaporative, evaporator and evaporated milk.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 evaporation、evaporative、evaporator 以及 evaporated milk（炼乳）。

normal.en: Laboratory collocations: evaporate the solvent, evaporate to dryness.
normal.cn: 实验室搭配：蒸去溶剂、蒸至干。

normal.en: The transitive form takes an object; the intransitive form takes from or into.
normal.cn: 及物形式带宾语；不及物形式常接 from 或 into。

normal.en: The figurative sense usually pairs with money, hope, support or anger.
normal.cn: 比喻义常与金钱、希望、支持或怒气搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a wet footprint on hot stone shrinking until only a pale shape is left.
abstract.cn: 想象炎热石板上一个湿脚印不断缩小，最后只剩浅色轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture a pot of soup simmering down while the kitchen window fogs up.
abstract.cn: 想象一锅汤慢慢收浓，厨房窗户同时蒙上水汽。

abstract.en: Picture a promise written in chalk and erased by rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一句用粉笔写下的承诺，被雨冲掉。

examples.en: The sun evaporates the last pools along the riverbed.
examples.cn: 太阳把河床上最后几处水洼蒸干。

examples.en: Heat evaporates the solvent, leaving a thin film of crystals.
examples.cn: 加热蒸去溶剂，留下一层薄薄的晶体。

examples.en: Public confidence evaporated after the third delay.
examples.cn: 第三次拖延之后，公众信心消散了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一娃泼水，越泼越少」——水在太阳下变少、消失 → 蒸发

root: 拉丁语 e-「向外」+ vaporare「冒汽」，源自 vapor「蒸汽、水汽」；经法语 évaporer 进入英语。vapor 更深来源不确定，比喻义首见年代存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the same change of state but vary the viewpoint: the process, its end point, the person doing it, the purpose, the abstract extension, the loss of intensity, the passive water cycle and the old emission reading.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次状态变化展开，只是视角不同：过程本身、终点、施动者、目的、抽象延伸、强度衰减、水循环中的被动失去，以及古老的「散发」读法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a film of moisture thinning under the sun until it is gone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层湿气在阳光下不断变薄，直到消失。

branches.en: PROCESS AND END: the change itself and the moment when no liquid remains.
branches.cn: 过程与终点：变化本身，以及液体不剩的时刻。

branches.en: TRANSITIVE PURPOSE: heating removes a solvent either to clean a material or to concentrate it.
branches.cn: 及物目的：加热除去溶剂，或为净化材料，或为浓缩。

branches.en: METAPHOR: money and anger behave like volatile liquids, one vanishing, one cooling.
branches.cn: 比喻：金钱与怒气都像挥发性液体，一个消失，一个降温。

branches.en: PASSIVE WATER CYCLE: water leaves soil and leaves without an agent.
branches.cn: 被动水循环：水从土壤和叶片离开，没有施动者。

branches.en: OLD EMISSION: the substance is seen as giving off vapor rather than changing into it.
branches.cn: 古老散发义：物质被看作放出水汽，而不是变成水汽。

intro.en: Evaporate is the verb in a Latin-derived family whose members divide the work of naming the process, the device and the result.
intro.cn: evaporate 是一个拉丁来源词族里的动词，族内成员分担命名过程、装置与结果。

latinIntro.en: Latin vapor and vaporare supply the base; e- marks movement out, and -ate marks the verb, while -ation and -or name the action and the device.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vapor 与 vaporare 提供基础；e- 标记向外，-ate 标记动词，而 -ation 与 -or 分别命名动作与装置。

items.example: The prefix sends the vapor outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把水汽送向外。

items.example: The base names what the liquid becomes.
items.exampleCN: 基础词命名液体变成之物。

items.meaning: the process or amount of evaporating
items.example: Evaporation removes water from the brine.
Evaporative cooling is effective in dry heat.
items.exampleCN: 干热环境下蒸发降温有效。

items.example: The evaporator coil chills the air.
items.exampleCN: 蒸发器盘管使空气变冷。

items.meaning: having been evaporated; thickened by evaporation
items.example: Evaporated milk keeps longer than fresh milk.
A vaporous mist covered the fields.
items.exampleCN: 一层雾状水汽覆盖田野。

items.example: The heat vaporizes the fuel before ignition.
items.exampleCN: 热量在点火前使燃料汽化。

definition_zh: 蒸发；蒸发量；蒸干浓缩
definition_en: the process by which a liquid changes into vapor at its surface, or the loss of moisture caused by this process
core_image: 一只浅盘里的水在阳光下越来越薄，盘底慢慢露出一圈白色的盐痕
scene: 雨后的水洼在午后阳光下缩小，傍晚只剩一圈浅浅的湿痕。 A shallow puddle shrinks under the afternoon sun, and by evening only a damp ring remains: that steady loss of water is evaporation.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「液体在表面缓慢变成水汽而减少」（第 1 个义项：液面汽化）；句意为水洼在阳光下缩小，到傍晚只剩湿痕，这种持续失水就是蒸发。

pos.zh: 蒸干；通过蒸发使溶液浓缩

forms.label: 复数（多种蒸发过程或多次测定）

senses.title: Liquid turning into vapor
senses.definition: the process in which molecules at the surface of a liquid escape into the air as vapor
senses.definitionCN: 液体表面分子逸入空气、变成水汽的过程
senses.example: Evaporation from the open tank continues even when the water is cool.
senses.exampleCN: 即使水是凉的，敞口罐里的水仍在持续蒸发。
senses.why: Only surface molecules can leave; the liquid does not need to boil. This is the physical core of the word.
senses.whyCN: 只有表面分子能逃出去，液体不必沸腾。这是这个词的物理核心。

senses.title: Loss of moisture from a surface
senses.definition: the drying of soil, skin, laundry or pavement as moisture leaves it
senses.definitionCN: 土壤、皮肤、衣物或路面因水分离开而变干
senses.example: Covering the seedbed slows evaporation and keeps the soil moist.
senses.exampleCN: 覆盖苗床能减缓蒸发，让土壤保持湿润。
senses.why: The same physical process seen from the side of the material: what matters is how much water it loses.
senses.whyCN: 同一个物理过程从材料一侧看：重点是它失去了多少水。

senses.title: Concentration by boiling off water
senses.definition: the removal of water by heating so that a solution becomes more concentrated
senses.definitionCN: 加热除去水分，使溶液变得更浓
senses.example: Salt is obtained from seawater by evaporation in shallow pans.
senses.exampleCN: 盐是通过在浅盘中蒸发海水得到的。
senses.why: Here evaporation is used as a tool: the water is unwanted, and what stays behind is the product.
senses.whyCN: 这里蒸发是工具：水是不要的部分，留下来的才是产物。

senses.title: Water-cycle flux
senses.definition: the movement of water from land and water bodies into the atmosphere, treated as a measurable part of the water cycle
senses.definitionCN: 水从陆地和有水表面进入大气，作为水循环中可测量的一环
senses.example: Satellites estimate evaporation over the ocean by tracking water vapor.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星通过追踪水汽来估算海面上的蒸发量。
senses.why: In earth science the process is treated as a flux: water leaves a surface at a measurable rate.
senses.whyCN: 在地球科学里，这一过程被当作通量：水以可测的速度离开某个表面。

senses.title: Amount evaporated
senses.definition: the quantity of water lost by evaporation, usually measured over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内因蒸发失去的水量
senses.example: The pan recorded an evaporation of four millimeters overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸发皿记录到一夜之间蒸发了四毫米。
senses.why: The process name is transferred to its measured result, a common pattern in scientific vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 过程名称被转用到测量结果上，这是科学词汇常见的转义方式。

senses.title: Vaporization below boiling
senses.definition: vaporization that occurs below the boiling point, especially in physics and engineering
senses.definitionCN: 在沸点以下发生的汽化，尤用于物理与工程
senses.example: Evaporation differs from boiling because it needs no bubbles.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸发与沸腾不同，因为它不需要气泡。
senses.why: Physics separates evaporation from boiling by mechanism, not by speed.
senses.whyCN: 物理学按机制而非速度把蒸发与沸腾区分开。

senses.title: Figurative disappearance
senses.definition: the gradual disappearance of money, support, confidence or another abstract quantity
senses.definitionCN: 钱、支持、信心等抽象之物的逐渐消失
senses.example: The evaporation of public trust followed the repeated delays.
senses.exampleCN: 反复拖延之后，公众信任逐渐消失。
senses.why: The metaphor treats an abstract quantity as a liquid that silently thins out.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把抽象之物当成一种无声变薄的液体。

senses.title: Evaporative cooling
senses.definition: cooling produced when a liquid evaporates and takes heat away with it
senses.definitionCN: 液体蒸发带走热量而产生的降温
senses.example: Sweating relies on evaporation to lower body temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 出汗依靠蒸发来降低体温。
senses.why: The word names the process that removes heat, so it also names the cooling effect used by organisms and machines.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是带走热量的过程，因此也指生物与机器利用的降温效果。

intro.en: The Latin elements are clear, but the deeper origin of vapor is disputed, and the dates of the technical senses are approximate.
intro.cn: 拉丁成分清楚，但 vapor 更深来源存在争议；技术义的出现年代为大致估计。

items.en: The base is vapor 'steam, vapor' with the verb vaporare 'to steam, to be hot'. The prefix e- (before a consonant, from ex-) means 'out of'.
items.cn: 基础词是 vapor「蒸汽、水汽」与动词 vaporare「冒汽、发热」。前缀 e-（辅音前由 ex- 变来）意为「向外」。

items.en: Late Latin evaporatio, evaporationis (f., third declension) meant 'a steaming away'. The noun is built from evaporare plus the action suffix -atio.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 evaporatio（属格 evaporationis，阴性第三变格）意为「蒸散」。该名词由 evaporare 加动作后缀 -atio 构成。

items.en: English adopted evaporation in the seventeenth century through scientific French and Latin. Early examples describe the drying of liquids.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪经科学法语与拉丁语吸收 evaporation，早期例子描述液体的变干。

items.en: With the growth of chemistry and meteorology, the noun acquired measured and technical uses such as evaporation rate and evaporation residue.
items.cn: 随着化学与气象学的发展，该名词获得「蒸发速率」「蒸发残渣」等测量与技术用法。

items.en: The figurative sense for money, trust or hope is a nineteenth- and twentieth-century extension. The underlying image is a liquid thinning until nothing is left.
items.cn: 用于金钱、信任或希望的比喻义是十九至二十世纪的延伸。底层意象是一种液体不断变薄，直到什么都不剩。

note.en: The first group is close in sound but not in root; the second group shares the physical process or its opposite.
note.cn: 第一组读音相近但不同源；第二组共享同一物理过程或其反面。

entries.definition: the act of moving people out of a dangerous place. It comes from Latin vacuus 'empty', not from vapor.
entries.definitionCN: 撤离；疏散。来自拉丁语 vacuus「空的」，与 vapor 无关。

entries.definition: the act of judging the value or quality of something, from Latin valere 'to be worth'.
entries.definitionCN: 评估；评价。来自拉丁语 valere「有价值」，与蒸发无关。

entries.definition: the combined loss of water by evaporation from the soil and transpiration from plants; it contains evaporation but adds the plant pathway.
entries.definitionCN: 蒸散。土壤蒸发与植物蒸腾之和；词里含 evaporation，但增加了植物这条路径。

entries.definition: the general change from liquid to vapor, including boiling; evaporation is the surface-only case.
entries.definitionCN: 汽化。液变气的一般过程，包括沸腾；蒸发只是仅发生在表面的那一种。

entries.definition: the change from vapor back to liquid; it is the reverse arrow of the water cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 凝结。水汽变回液体，是水循环里方向相反的一支。

entries.definition: the loss of water vapor through plant surfaces; it is evaporation routed through a living organism.
entries.definitionCN: 蒸腾。水汽经植物表面散失；可以理解为经过活体生物的蒸发。

entries.definition: the everyday word for becoming dry; it names the result rather than the physical mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 变干；干燥。日常词，说的是结果，而不是物理机制。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'out' and the base means 'steam': steam going out of a liquid.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「向外」，基础词意为「蒸汽」：蒸汽从液体里出去。

normal.en: The family runs evaporate, evaporative, evaporator and evapotranspiration.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 evaporate、evaporative、evaporator 与 evapotranspiration。

normal.en: Science fixes the collocations: evaporation rate, evaporation residue, evaporation pan.
normal.cn: 科学语境固定搭配：蒸发速率、蒸发残渣、蒸发皿。

normal.en: Evaporation is the surface process; boiling is the bulk process with bubbles.
normal.cn: 蒸发是表面过程；沸腾是整体过程并产生气泡。

normal.en: The water cycle pairs evaporation with condensation and precipitation.
normal.cn: 水循环把蒸发与凝结、降水配成一组。

abstract.en: Picture a shallow plate of water slowly turning into a white ring of salt.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘浅水慢慢变成一圈白色的盐痕。

abstract.en: Picture a bank balance shrinking without any withdrawal being recorded.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔存款没有任何取款记录却不断变少。

abstract.en: Picture a puddle that leaves only a dark outline on the pavement.
abstract.cn: 想象一洼水最后只在路面上留下一个深色轮廓。

examples.en: Evaporation from the lake leaves a crust of salt along the shore.
examples.cn: 湖水的蒸发在岸边留下一层盐壳。

examples.en: Mulch reduces evaporation and helps seedlings survive a dry spell.
examples.cn: 覆盖物减少蒸发，帮助幼苗熬过干旱期。

examples.en: The evaporation of the reserve fund was never explained to members.
examples.cn: 储备金的逐渐消失从未向成员解释过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一娃泼水」——泼出去的水在太阳下慢慢变少 → 蒸发

root: 拉丁语 e-「向外」+ vaporare「冒汽」，源自 vapor「蒸汽、水汽」；经晚期拉丁语 evaporatio 与科学法语进入英语。vapor 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from one physical event and fan out into measurement, technique and metaphor. The event is surface escape; measurement turns it into a number, technique turns it into a tool, and metaphor turns it into silent loss.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个物理事件出发，再分向测量、技术与比喻。事件本身是表面逸出；测量把它变成数字，技术把它变成工具，比喻把它变成无声的流失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin layer of liquid losing itself into the air, leaving a mark behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层薄液不断进入空气，最后留下痕迹。

branches.en: ESCAPE AND DRYING: the same event seen from the air side and from the material side.
branches.cn: 逸出与变干：同一事件从空气一侧和材料一侧分别看。

branches.en: CONCENTRATION: removing water is a tool, and physics names its mechanism.
branches.cn: 浓缩：除去水分是一种工具，物理学为其机制命名。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: the water cycle turns the event into a flux and then into a number.
branches.cn: 测量：水循环把事件变成通量，再变成数字。

branches.en: COOLING: the escaping molecules carry heat, so evaporation becomes a service.
branches.cn: 降温：逃出的分子带走热量，蒸发于是成为一种功能。

branches.en: METAPHOR: an abstract quantity is treated as a liquid that thins away.
branches.cn: 比喻：抽象之物被当作一种会变薄的液体。

intro.en: Evaporation is built from Latin pieces that also build a compact English family, so the word can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: evaporation 由拉丁成分构成，这些成分还构成一组紧凑的英语词族，因此可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin vapor gives vapor, vaporous and evaporate; the prefix e- marks movement out, and -atio marks an action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vapor 衍生 vapor、vaporous 与 evaporate；前缀 e- 标记「向外」，后缀 -atio 标记动作或其结果。

latinEntries.meaning: to steam away, to pass off as vapor

items.example: The prefix marks water leaving the liquid.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记水离开液体。

items.example: The base names the thing that the liquid becomes.
items.exampleCN: 基础词命名液体变成的东西。

items.meaning: the action or result of steaming away
items.exampleCN: 蒸发使剩余的液体降温。

items.example: The puddle will evaporate by noon.
Evaporative cooling works in dry air.
items.exampleCN: 蒸发降温在干燥空气中有效。

items.meaning: a device that evaporates a liquid
items.example: The evaporator removes water from the juice.
items.exampleCN: 蒸发器除去果汁中的水。

items.meaning: combined water loss from soil and plants
items.example: Evapotranspiration is measured over whole catchments.
items.exampleCN: 蒸散在整个流域尺度上测量。

items.example: A vaporous haze hung over the warm marsh.
items.exampleCN: 温暖沼泽上方悬着一层雾状水汽。

items.example: The laser can vaporize a thin metal film.
items.exampleCN: 激光能使薄金属膜汽化。

definition_zh: 甚至；连……都；平坦的；均匀的；偶数的
definition_en: used to stress something surprising, or describing something flat, regular or equal
core_image: 一条完全水平的地面，无论怎么走都没有高低起伏
scene: 他忙了一整天，甚至连午饭都忘了吃。He was busy all day and even forgot to eat lunch.
sceneCN: 这里 even 是「甚至」（第 1 个义项：用来强调出人意料的情况）；句意：他忙了一整天，甚至连午饭都忘了吃。

senses.title: Used for emphasis
senses.definition: used to stress something that is surprising or extreme
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调令人意外或极端的情况
senses.example: He even brought flowers to the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他甚至带花来开会。
senses.why: The emphatic use grows from the idea of equality: this case is as true as the others.
senses.whyCN: 强调用法来自「同等」的观念：这种情况与其余情况一样真实。

senses.title: Flat and level
senses.definition: flat and level, with no higher or lower parts
senses.definitionCN: 平坦水平，没有高低起伏
senses.example: The table has an even surface.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌面很平。
senses.why: The oldest sense is level, where every point has the same height.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是水平，即每一点高度相同。

senses.title: Regular and equal
senses.definition: regular, equal or balanced in amount or spacing
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或间隔上规则、相等或均衡
senses.example: Spread the paint in an even layer.
senses.exampleCN: 把颜料涂成均匀的一层。
senses.why: Equal height becomes equal amount when applied more widely.
senses.whyCN: 把「等高的」扩展到更广范围，就是「等量的」。

senses.title: Divisible by two
senses.definition: a number that can be divided by two exactly
senses.definitionCN: 能被二整除的数
senses.example: Two, four and six are even numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 二、四、六都是偶数。
senses.why: An even number splits into two equal halves, matching the idea of balance.
senses.whyCN: 偶数能分成两个相等的半，符合均衡的观念。

senses.title: Make equal
senses.definition: to make something equal or level
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物相等或平坦
senses.example: The final goal evened the score.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一个进球把比分扳平了。
senses.why: The verb turns the adjective into the act of making things level.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「平的」变成「使变平」的动作。

intro.en: Even comes from Old English efen, meaning level or equal.
intro.cn: even 源自古英语 efen（平的、相等的）。

items.en: Efen means level or equal.
items.cn: efen 意为平坦或相等。

items.en: Even describes flat ground and equal shares.
items.cn: even 描述平地与均等的份额。

items.en: The word also names numbers divisible by two.
items.cn: 这个词也指能被二整除的数。

items.en: As an adverb it adds emphasis.
items.cn: 作副词时它增加强调。

items.en: Even though and even if mark contrast.
items.cn: even though 与 even if 标记让步对比。

note.en: Even is a common word with level, equal and emphatic uses.
note.cn: even 是常用词，兼有平坦、相等与强调的用法。

entries.definition: in an equal way
the state of being level
not level or regular
flat and not sloping
the same in size or amount
used to add emphasis

normalIntro.en: Even begins with a level line: flat ground, equal shares, balanced numbers.
normalIntro.cn: even 从一条水平线开始：平地、均分、平衡的数字。

normal.en: Even though introduces a fact that does not change the result.
normal.cn: even though 引出一个不改变结果的事实。

normal.en: Even if imagines a case that may not happen.
normal.cn: even if 想象一种可能不发生的假设。

normal.en: An even surface has no bumps.
normal.cn: an even surface 没有凸起。

normal.en: An even number divides into two equal parts.
normal.cn: 偶数能分成两个相等的部分。

normal.en: Compare level: level stresses height, even stresses lack of variation.
normal.cn: 对比 level：level 强调高度，even 强调没有变化。

abstract.en: Picture a calm lake with no waves.
abstract.cn: 想象一片没有波浪的平静湖面。

abstract.en: Imagine a rope pulled straight and taut.
abstract.cn: 想象一根被拉得笔直紧绷的绳子。

abstract.en: Think of two children sharing a cake equally.
abstract.cn: 想象两个孩子平均分一块蛋糕。

examples.en: She even forgot her own birthday.
examples.cn: 她甚至忘了自己的生日。

examples.en: The ground is not even enough for a tent.
examples.cn: 地面不够平，搭不了帐篷。

examples.en: Cut the bread into even slices.
examples.cn: 把面包切成厚度均匀的片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「even」有「一平」的感觉——平平整整、不多不少，于是也有「甚至」的强调；这只是联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 efen（平的、相等的）→ even，核心义「没有高低差别、彼此相等」。

sensesIntro.en: Even starts with emphasis, then describes flat surfaces, regular amounts, numbers split in two, and the act of making things equal.
sensesIntro.cn: even 从强调用法开始，再指平坦表面、均匀数量、可对分的数字，以及使事物相等的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a perfectly level line with no bumps.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条完全没有起伏的水平线。

branches.en: The adverb adds surprising emphasis.
branches.cn: 副词增加出人意料的强调。

branches.en: A flat surface has the same height throughout.
branches.cn: 平坦表面处处同高。

branches.en: Regular spacing and amount extend the flat idea.
branches.cn: 规则的间隔与数量延伸了「平」的概念。

branches.en: Even numbers split into two equal halves.
branches.cn: 偶数能分成两个相等的半。

branches.en: The verb makes a score or surface level.
branches.cn: 动词使比分或表面变平。

intro.en: Even is a native Old English word and takes suffixes such as -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: even 是古英语本族词，可加 -ly、-ness 等后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源。

items.example: Though combines with even to mark contrast.
items.exampleCN: though 与 even 组合表示让步对比。

items.example: If combines with even for a hypothetical case.
items.exampleCN: if 与 even 组合表示假设情况。

definition_zh: 事件；活动；赛事
definition_en: something that happens, especially something important or planned
core_image: 日历上的一个圆圈，把某一天紧紧标了出来
scene: 这场音乐节是城里一年中最大的文化活动。This music festival is the city's biggest cultural event of the year.
sceneCN: 这里 event 是「活动」（第 2 个义项：有组织、按计划举行的场合）；句意：这场音乐节是城里一年中最大的文化活动。

senses.title: Something that happens
senses.definition: something that happens, especially something important
senses.definitionCN: 发生的事情，尤其是重要的事
senses.example: The discovery was a major event in science.
senses.exampleCN: 这一发现是科学界的重大事件。
senses.why: The Latin source means an outcome, so an event is what comes out of a situation.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为结果，因此事件就是从某种情况中产生的事。

senses.title: A planned occasion
senses.definition: an organized occasion such as a party or festival
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的场合，如聚会或节日庆典
senses.example: The charity holds a fund-raising event each year.
senses.exampleCN: 该慈善机构每年举办一次筹款活动。
senses.why: An occasion planned in advance is an event on the calendar.
senses.whyCN: 提前计划的场合就是日历上的一件活动。

senses.title: A sports contest
senses.definition: one of the races or competitions in a sports meeting
senses.definitionCN: 运动会中的一项比赛
senses.example: The long jump is her best event.
senses.exampleCN: 跳远是她最擅长的项目。
senses.why: A single contest is one scheduled happening within a larger meeting.
senses.whyCN: 单项比赛是大型运动会中安排的一次具体发生。

intro.en: Event comes from Latin eventus, an outcome, from evenire, to come out.
intro.cn: event 源自拉丁语 eventus（结果），来自 evenire（出来、发生）。

items.en: Evenire means to come out or happen.
items.cn: evenire 意为出来或发生。

items.en: Eventus means an outcome.
items.cn: eventus 意为结果。

items.en: Evenement means something that happens.
items.cn: evenement 意为发生的事。

items.en: Event covers important happenings.
items.cn: event 涵盖重要事件。

items.en: It also names planned occasions and contests.
items.cn: 它也指计划好的活动与比赛。

note.en: Event is close to incident and occasion, and is broader than either.
note.cn: event 与事件、场合相近，但比两者都宽泛。

entries.definition: full of happenings
quiet and ordinary
a possible happening
an unusual or unpleasant event
a time when something happens
an event or situation

normalIntro.en: An event is a date circled on the calendar: something happens there.
normalIntro.cn: event 就是日历上被圈出的日子：那天有事情发生。

normal.en: A major event is important enough to remember.
normal.cn: major event 重要到值得记住。

normal.en: A sporting event draws a crowd.
normal.cn: sporting event 会吸引人群。

normal.en: In the event of rain means if rain happens.
normal.cn: in the event of rain 意为如果下雨。

normal.en: Current events are recent news happenings.
normal.cn: current events 是近期新闻事件。

normal.en: Compare incident: an incident is usually small or unpleasant, an event can be planned.
normal.cn: 对比 incident：incident 通常较小或不愉快，event 可以是计划好的。

abstract.en: Picture one day on a calendar circled in red.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上有一天被红笔圈出。

abstract.en: Imagine a stage waiting for a crowd to arrive.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台等待人群到来。

abstract.en: Think of a page of news filled with big headlines.
abstract.cn: 想象一页写满大标题的新闻。

examples.en: The wedding was the biggest event of the year.
examples.cn: 婚礼是那一年最大的事件。

examples.en: She helped organize a charity event.
examples.cn: 她帮忙组织了一场慈善活动。

examples.en: The team won three events at the games.
examples.cn: 该队在运动会上赢得了三个项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「event」听起来像「一万一」——值得记下的大事；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 e-（出）＋ venire（来）→ evenire（发生）→ eventus（结果）→ event，核心义「从情况中产生、发生的事情」。

sensesIntro.en: Event first names anything that happens, then a planned occasion, and finally one contest in a sports meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: event 先指发生的任何事，再指计划好的场合，最后指运动会中的单项比赛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a day circled on a calendar.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上被圈出的一天。

branches.en: Anything important that happens is an event.
branches.cn: 发生的任何重要事情都是事件。

branches.en: Planned occasions are events on a schedule.
branches.cn: 计划好的场合是日程上的活动。

branches.en: One contest is an event within a meeting.
branches.cn: 单项比赛是运动会中的一项赛事。

branches.en: A planned event becomes a remembered happening.
branches.cn: 计划好的活动会成为被记住的事件。

branches.en: Sports meetings are events made of events.
branches.cn: 运动会是由多项赛事组成的活动。

intro.en: Event comes from Latin evenire, to come out, with the noun ending -tus.
intro.cn: event 源自拉丁语 evenire（出来、发生），带名词词尾 -tus。

latinIntro.en: Latin venire, to come, gives event, prevent and invent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 venire（来）衍生出 event、prevent 与 invent。

items.exampleCN: eventful 描述忙碌多事的时期。

definition_zh: 永久的；没完没了的；永生花；永恒
definition_en: lasting for ever, or going on for so long that it seems it will never stop
core_image: 窗台上那束花放了很多年，颜色一点也没退
scene: 老人把一束干花放在窗台上，那是很多年前婚礼上留下来的。She kept the everlasting flowers in a glass jar beside the window.
sceneCN: 这里 everlasting 是「永生花」（第 3 个义项：经过处理、多年不谢的花）；句意：她把永生花装进玻璃瓶，摆在窗边。

derivatives.zh: 由 everlasting 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「永久；永恒」
由动词 last 加 -ing 构成，义为「持久的」，是 everlasting 的后半部分
「持续；延续」，是 lasting 与 everlasting 共同的动词词基

senses.title: Lasting for ever
senses.definition: continuing for all time, with no end
senses.definitionCN: 一直持续下去，没有尽头
senses.example: They promised each other everlasting friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 他们许诺给彼此永远的友谊。
senses.why: Ever means at any time and lasting means continuing, so the compound says continuing at every time.
senses.whyCN: ever 表示「在任何时候」，lasting 表示「持续」，两者相加就是「在任何时候都持续」，所以是永久。

senses.title: Going on far too long
senses.titleCN: 没完没了的；拖得太久的
senses.definition: seeming to continue for too long and becoming annoying
senses.definitionCN: 显得持续太久而让人厌烦
senses.example: The everlasting rain in that town wears everyone down.
senses.exampleCN: 那座镇上没完没了的雨把人磨得疲惫不堪。
senses.why: The same never-ending time is now aimed at things people must sit through, so praise turns into complaint.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「永不结束」的意思被用在人不得不忍受的事情上，褒义就变成了抱怨，于是有了「没完没了」。

senses.title: A preserved flower
senses.definition: a flower that has been treated so that it keeps its shape and colour for years
senses.definitionCN: 经过处理、多年仍保持形状与颜色的花
senses.example: She dried the roses to make everlasting flowers.
senses.exampleCN: 她把玫瑰干燥处理，做成了永生花。
senses.why: A treated flower really does hold its colour for years, so the adjective of endless time is borrowed as the name of the object.
senses.whyCN: 处理过的花确实能多年保住颜色，于是表示「时间无尽」的形容词被直接借来给这种花命名。

senses.title: The endless state itself
senses.definition: endless time or endless existence, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 无尽的时间或无尽的存在，作名词使用
senses.example: The poem speaks of the everlasting rather than of this short life.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗谈的是永恒，而不是这短暂的一生。
senses.why: English turns adjectives into nouns with the definite article, so the everlasting can name the endless state itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用定冠词把形容词变成名词，the everlasting 就用来指「永恒」这个状态本身。

intro.en: Everlasting is a native English compound of ever and lasting, and both halves go back to Old English.
intro.cn: everlasting 是英语本族语的复合词，由 ever 与 lasting 组成，两部分都可上溯到古英语。

items.en: Ǣfre means at any time, or always.
items.cn: 古英语 ǣfre 意为「在任何时候、永远」。

items.en: Lǣstan means to follow, to carry out, or to endure.
items.cn: lǣstan 意为跟随、执行，也表示持续。

items.en: Ever and lasting are joined, and the compound is recorded from about the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语把 ever 与 lasting 拼合，这个复合词约在十三世纪见于记录。

items.en: The word is also used as a noun naming eternity.
items.cn: 十四世纪起，这个词也作名词，指永恒。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective of endless time and adds the name of the preserved flower.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「时间无尽」的形容词用法，又添上永生花这个名称。

note.en: Everlasting belongs to the ever family and stands beside the eternal words.
note.cn: everlasting 属于 ever 词族，并与表示「永恒」的一批词相邻。

entries.definition: continuing for a long time
at any time, or always
for all time to come
lasting for ever, with no beginning and no end
continuing without stopping
having no end or limit

normalIntro.en: Everlasting is built from two plain English words: ever and lasting.
normalIntro.cn: everlasting 由两个普通英语词拼成：ever 与 lasting。

normal.en: Ever means at all times.
normal.cn: ever 表示「在任何时候」。

normal.en: Lasting means continuing.
normal.cn: lasting 表示「持续」。

normal.en: Everlasting peace is peace that never ends.
normal.cn: everlasting peace 指永不结束的和平。

normal.en: Everlasting fame outlives the person who earned it.
normal.cn: everlasting fame 指人不在之后仍然留下的名声。

normal.en: Compare eternal: eternal is more abstract and formal, while everlasting is plainer.
normal.cn: 对比 eternal：它更抽象、更正式，everlasting 更朴素。

abstract.en: Picture a candle that never burns down.
abstract.cn: 想象一支永远烧不完的蜡烛。

abstract.en: Imagine a song stuck on one line that will not stop.
abstract.cn: 想象一首歌卡在同一句上，怎么也停不下来。

abstract.en: Think of a rose sealed in resin, still red after many years.
abstract.cn: 想象一朵封在树脂里的玫瑰，许多年后仍然鲜红。

examples.en: They promised each other everlasting friendship.
examples.cn: 他们许诺给彼此永远的友谊。

examples.en: The everlasting rain in that town wears everyone down.
examples.cn: 那座镇上没完没了的雨把人磨得疲惫不堪。

examples.en: She dried the roses to make everlasting flowers.
examples.cn: 她把玫瑰干燥处理，做成了永生花。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱我 lasting」：说要爱我一直到最后，就成了永久。这只是谐音联想，并不是真正的词源。

root: ever（任何时候）+ lasting（持续的）→ everlasting（永久的）→ 引申为「没完没了」，名词再指永生花；核心义是「时间上没有尽头」。

sensesIntro.en: Everlasting starts as endless time, turns into a complaint about things that drag on, and ends by naming a flower that keeps its colour.
sensesIntro.cn: everlasting 先指没有尽头的时间，再用来抱怨拖得太久的事，最后指一种久不褪色的花。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flower on the windowsill that never dries out.
core.cn: 核心意象：窗台上一朵永不枯萎的花。

branches.en: Endless time is the core adjective sense.
branches.cn: 时间无尽是核心的形容词义项。

branches.en: The same endlessness becomes a complaint when a thing drags on.
branches.cn: 同一份「无尽」用在拖沓的事情上，就成了抱怨。

branches.en: A preserved flower carries the endlessness into an object name.
branches.cn: 永生花把「无尽」带进了一个实物名称。

branches.en: The noun names the endless state itself.
branches.cn: 名词义项直接指「永恒」这个状态。

branches.en: Both the adjective and the flower name promise that colour and time hold still.
branches.cn: 形容词与花名都许诺颜色与时间停住不动。

intro.en: Everlasting is a transparent English compound: ever plus lasting, with -ness and -ly building further words.
intro.cn: everlasting 是一个透明的英语复合词：ever 加 lasting，再由 -ness 与 -ly 构成新词。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Germanic rather than Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list here.
latinIntro.cn: 两个组成部分都属日耳曼语，不来自拉丁语，因此这里没有拉丁同源词可列。

items.example: Ever is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: ever 是复合词的前一半。

items.example: Lasting describes what goes on and on.
items.exampleCN: lasting 描述持续不断的事物。

items.example: The verb last is the base of lasting.
items.exampleCN: 动词 last 是 lasting 的词基。

items.example: Lǣstan is the Old English source of last.
items.exampleCN: lǣstan 是 last 的古英语来源。

items.example: Ǣfre is the Old English source of ever.
items.exampleCN: ǣfre 是 ever 的古英语来源。

items.meaningCN: 把动词变成形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing turns last into lasting.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 把 last 变成 lasting。

items.meaningCN: 把形容词变成名词的词尾

items.meaning: the state of lasting for ever
items.example: Everlastingness is the noun of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: everlastingness 是这个形容词的名词形式。

definition_zh: 证据；迹象
definition_en: facts or signs that show something is true
core_image: 桌上摆着放大镜、照片和一叠文件
scene: 警方在窗台上发现一枚指纹，这成为案件的关键证据。Police found a fingerprint on the windowsill, and it became the key evidence in the case.
sceneCN: 这里 evidence 是「证据」（第 1 个义项：帮助证明某事的事实）；句意：警方在窗台上发现一枚指纹，这成为案件的关键证据。

senses.title: Proof in a case
senses.definition: facts that help prove something
senses.definitionCN: 帮助证明某事的事实
senses.example: The police collected evidence at the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在现场收集证据。
senses.why: Evidence is what makes a claim visible and clear.
senses.whyCN: 证据让主张变得可见而清楚。

senses.title: A sign
senses.definition: a sign that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 表明某事属实的迹象
senses.example: There is evidence of rain in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 山里有下雨的迹象。
senses.why: The word extends from courts to ordinary observation.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从法庭延伸到日常观察。

senses.title: To show
senses.definition: to show or prove something
senses.definitionCN: 表明或证明某事
senses.example: The results evidence a clear improvement.

definition_zh: 唤起；引起；使人想起；召唤
definition_en: to bring a memory, feeling, or image into the mind, or to call something up
core_image: 一只手从记忆的深井里把旧画面提上来
scene: 旧相册摊在桌上，屋里一下子安静了。The old photograph evoked a summer that nobody in the room had mentioned for years.
sceneCN: 这里 evoke 是「唤起、使人想起」（第 1 个义项：把记忆或画面带回心里）；句意：那张旧照片唤起了屋里谁都没再提起的一个夏天。

senses.title: To call a memory to mind
senses.definition: to bring a memory or an image back into the mind
senses.definitionCN: 把记忆或画面重新带回某人心里
senses.example: The smell of fresh bread evokes the kitchen of his grandmother.
senses.exampleCN: 新鲜面包的气味唤起他祖母的厨房。
senses.why: Latin vocare means to call and the prefix e- means out, so to evoke is to call a memory out of where it was kept.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vocare 意为「叫」，前缀 e- 意为「出」，所以 evoke 就是把记忆从存放它的地方叫出来。

senses.title: To cause a feeling or reaction
senses.definition: to produce a feeling, an answer, or a reaction in other people
senses.definitionCN: 在别人身上产生某种情感、回答或反应
senses.example: Her calm voice evoked no panic in the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 她平静的声音没有在人群中引起恐慌。
senses.why: What is called out need not be a memory; a feeling can be called out too, so the verb widens from remembering to causing.
senses.whyCN: 被「叫出来」的不一定是记忆，情绪也能被叫出来，于是这个词从「想起」扩展到「引起」。

senses.title: To remind someone of something
senses.definition: to make people think of a particular thing or person
senses.definitionCN: 让人联想到某个特定的事物或人
senses.example: A single word can evoke a whole summer.
senses.exampleCN: 一个词就能唤起整个夏天。
senses.why: If one thing calls another to mind, the verb can name that link itself and not just the act of remembering.
senses.whyCN: 如果一物把另一物叫到心里，这个词就能指这种联想关系，而不只是回忆的动作。

senses.title: To call up a spirit
senses.definition: to call a spirit or a god to appear, used in older and literary writing
senses.definitionCN: 把神灵叫出来现身，多用于较古的或文学性的文字
senses.example: In the old story the priest evokes the dead at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个古老的故事里，祭司在午夜召唤亡者。
senses.why: The oldest use is a literal calling out to a spirit, and that religious sense survives in literary English.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法就是字面地把神灵叫出来，这个宗教含义在文学语言里保留了下来。

intro.en: Evoke comes from Latin evocare, built from e-, out, and vocare, to call, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: evoke 来自拉丁语 evocare，由 e-（出）与 vocare（叫）构成，并经法语进入英语。

items.cn: evocare 把 e-（出）与 vocare（叫）合在一起，意为叫出来。

items.en: Evocare also names the calling up of the spirits of the dead.
items.cn: evocare 也指把亡者的灵魂召唤出来。

items.en: The verb evoquer carries the word toward English.
items.cn: 古法语动词 evoquer 把这个词带向英语。

items.en: English adopts the verb in the seventeenth century as a word for calling something up.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入这个动词，用来指把某物唤出来。

items.en: Modern English extends it to memories, images, and reactions.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到记忆、画面与反应。

note.cn: evoke 属于拉丁语 vocare 词族，也属于「回忆、引起」这一语义场。

definition_zh: 进化；逐渐发展；释放
definition_en: to change slowly into a new form
core_image: 一颗种子在四季里长成开花的树
scene: 这株植物为了适应干旱，逐渐演化出更厚的叶片。The plant evolved thicker leaves in order to survive the drought.
sceneCN: 这里 evolve 是「逐渐演化」（第 1 个义项：生物经过世代发展出新特征）；句意：这株植物为了适应干旱，逐渐演化出更厚的叶片。

senses.title: Biological change
senses.definition: to develop new features over generations
senses.definitionCN: 经过许多世代发展出新特征
senses.example: Birds evolved from small dinosaurs.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟类由小型恐龙进化而来。
senses.why: Evolvere means to unroll, as a species unfolds over time.

senses.title: Gradual development
senses.definition: to develop slowly

senses.exampleCN: 计划逐渐发展成一个完整项目。
senses.why: Any idea can unfold like a living form.
senses.whyCN: 任何想法都能像生命形态一样展开。

senses.title: To give off

senses.exampleCN: 反应释放出刺鼻的气味。
senses.why: Unrolling can mean letting something out.
senses.whyCN: 展开也可以指让某物释放出来。
